subject: Dedicated capacity SLA — throughput & queueing exception for Brightside
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@brightside.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@brightside.ai>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 14:02 -0500
Subject: Questions on Dedicated capacity SLA: throughput guarantees & queueing

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We had a follow-up with our infrastructure team and they pushed back on a couple of SLA items before legal will sign the amendment:

- Can you confirm the throughput guarantees for Dedicated? We need a clear statement of concurrent streams (or RPS) for a pinned pool (we're evaluating 8 vs 16 GPUs).
- What happens when we hit queueing during a burst? Is there a hard rejection, or does your runtime queue requests? If queued, what's the max queue time and how is it surfaced to the caller (HTTP 202? retry headers?).
- If we request an SLA exception for a tighter p95 latency (for a specific model family and 512-token requests), what is the process for approval and what operational mitigations are available?

I've attached our initial SLA request doc with expected QPS and peak patterns. We're trying to avoid surprises in production (esp. around scheduled maintenance and cross-tenant noisy neighbors).

Appreciate a short summary we can hand to legal and infra.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Director of Platform
Brightside AI

[Attachment: Brightside_SLA_Request.pdf (PDF, 245KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@brightside.ai>
Cc: Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@brightside.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 15:10 -0500
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated capacity SLA: throughput guarantees & queueing

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by next steps:

- Throughput: for a pinned 8-GPU A100 pool we typically guarantee sustained throughput equivalent to ~200 concurrent inference streams for standard decoder-only models at typical prompt lengths (512 tokens). We can provide formal RPS/throughput numbers per model after we run a short benchmarking run against your prompt mix.
- Queueing behavior: Redwood will queue requests to preserve request completion rather than immediately rejecting. We operate a soft-queue with a configurable max wait (default 30s). If the queue exceeds the configured threshold, new requests are rejected with a 429 and a Retry-After header. Long queues are surfaced via Console metrics and a per-request header X-Redwood-Queue-Time.
- SLA exception process: exceptions for tighter p95 latency are handled by an Ops review + pilot (usually 2–4 weeks). We'll define a workload contract (prompt sets, token distributions) and recommend sizing + burst capacity. Exceptions include operational commitments (reserved GPU count, increased monitoring, runbook).

I've looped in Laura to capture any operational caveats and Aditya/Grace for provisioning/contract notes. I'm also attaching a proposed mutual action plan we can tweak together. If you want, we can run a 48–72 hour benchmark on your prompt set to convert our estimate into firm numbers.

Next step: Laura, can you confirm whether Ops will approve a 30s soft-queue and what a tighter p95 exception would require from an infra perspective?

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Proposed_MAPlan.xlsx (Excel, 85KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@brightside.ai>, Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@brightside.ai>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 09:45 -0500
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated capacity SLA: throughput guarantees & queueing

Vivek / team —

Thanks for looping ops in. Some operational specifics and clarifications from infra:

1) Reserved GPUs and throughput
- An 8xA100 reserved pool (no multi-tenant oversubscription) will, for your stated model family, reliably support ~180–220 concurrent short-form streams (512-token window) with p95 latency targets in our standard config. Exact numbers depend on batchability and kv-cache reuse; the benchmark Vivek suggested will firm this up.

2) Queueing & preemption
- We use a two-tier queuing policy: soft queue (default max 30s) where requests are buffered and prioritized by SLA class; when the soft queue exceeds capacity, incoming requests get a 429 + Retry-After.
- For Dedicated pools with burst capacity enabled, we allow short bursts (up to 20% extra capacity for ~5min windows) by temporarily borrowing from reserved burst slots; beyond that a 429 occurs.
- Preemption: lower-priority/hosted-tire workloads may be preempted during extreme contention if your policy opts into cost-saving preemption. For guaranteed latency exceptions, preemption is disabled for the dedicated pool during the exception window.

3) SLA exception (tighter p95)
- Requirements: dedicated benchmark run, a signed amendment that lists the workload contract (prompt sets, token distribution), reserved GPU count, and a runbook + incident response SLOs.
- Operational mitigations: dedicated monitoring (per-request tracing), on-call escalation to infra, extended retention for logs/metrics for 90 days, and a canary rollout for the exception period.
- Approval path: Ops + Legal + Support leadership sign-off. Typical turnaround 3–7 business days after benchmark results.

4) Maintenance & maintenance windows
- Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded from uptime calculations. We provide a 72-hour notification for non-emergency maintenance. For mission-critical exceptions we can negotiate blackout windows or arrange a temporary shadow pool.

I'll attach a short ops notes file with the configuration knobs we typically include in the amendment.

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Dedicated Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: reserved_capacity_ops_notes.txt (plain text, 3KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@brightside.ai>
Cc: Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@brightside.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 11:22 -0500
Subject: Final proposal: Dedicated SLA amendment & next steps

Samantha / Mike —

Following the ops input, here's a concise summary of what Redwood can commit in the amendment and the immediate next steps:

Committed (for Brightside AI, pending signed amendment):
- Uptime: 99.95% uptime SLA for the dedicated pool (excludes pre-notified maintenance windows and agreed blackout exceptions).
- Throughput: For an 8xA100 reserved pool we will commit to supporting 200 concurrent inference streams (512-token profile) as a baseline; we'll run the 48–72 hour benchmark on your prompt set to convert to exact RPS figures.
- Latency: Standard p95 SLO will be provided; for the requested tighter p95 exception we will:
  * Require signed amendment + benchmark run;
  * Disable preemption for the dedicated pool during the exception window;
  * Provide per-request tracing and 90-day metric/log retention;
  * Implement increased monitoring and a dedicated on-call rotation during the pilot.
- Queueing behavior: Soft queue enabled by default (max 30s). Exceeding the queue triggers 429 + Retry-After. Burst policy: up to 20% extra capacity for short bursts (~5 minutes) by design; beyond that, requests are rejected. X-Redwood-Queue-Time header will be present on responses when queued.

Exceptions & operational notes:
- We can approve a p95 latency exception for Brightside subject to the benchmark and approval workflow. Exceptions will include clear workload contracts and a short canary period (2 weeks) with rollback criteria.
- Scheduled maintenance and emergency repairs are excluded from uptime calculations; we'll provide 72-hour standard notice for planned work.

Next steps:
1) We (Redwood) run a 48–72 hour benchmark on your prompt set (you to provide a short sample and expected token distribution).
2) Legal review the amendment; I'm attaching the draft SLA amendment for initial review.
3) If acceptable, sign via DocuSign (link below) and we'll schedule provisioning + pilot.

Best regards,
